title: The Weight of Responsibility
text:
Responsibility is often discussed as a personal virtue, yet its boundaries become far less clear when decisions affect entire communities. Engineers who design a bridge, for instance, bear a duty that extends well beyond their employer, because the public will rely on their judgement for decades. Ethical responsibility therefore cannot be reduced to obeying instructions, since those who follow orders may still be held accountable for the harm they help to cause.

In recent years, organisations have attempted to formalise this duty through codes of conduct and independent oversight. Critics argue that such measures can become a form of reassurance rather than genuine accountability, particularly when penalties are rarely enforced. A more durable approach, many philosophers suggest, would cultivate a habit of asking who might be affected by a decision before it is made, rather than after the damage has occurred.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why does an engineer who designs a bridge have a duty that extends beyond their employer?
options: Because the public will rely on their judgement for decades
Because employers rarely pay them for their work
Because bridges must always be redesigned after ten years
Because engineering codes forbid working for private companies

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do critics say about codes of conduct and independent oversight?
options: They have replaced all legal penalties
They can become reassurance rather than genuine accountability
They have been shown to prevent every kind of harm

questions.text: What does the author imply about people who only follow orders?
options: They are never responsible for the results of their actions
They may still bear responsibility for harm they help to cause
They are usually unaware of the consequences of their work
They should be excused whenever a superior gives instructions

questions.text: What can be inferred about the approach favoured by many philosophers in the final sentence?
options: It focuses on punishing people after harm has already happened
It relies mainly on written rules enforced by governments
It encourages considering the effects of a decision before acting
It suggests that responsibility should be avoided where possible

vocabulary.definition: the ability to form sensible opinions and make decisions
required to explain one's actions and accept the consequences
something that removes doubt or fear
lasting for a long time without becoming weak

paragraph_translations: La responsabilidad suele debatirse como una virtud personal, pero sus límites se vuelven mucho menos claros cuando las decisiones afectan a comunidades enteras. Los ingenieros que diseñan un puente, por ejemplo, tienen un deber que va mucho más allá de su empleador, porque el público confiará en su juicio durante décadas. Por tanto, la responsabilidad ética no puede reducirse a obedecer instrucciones, ya que quienes siguen órdenes pueden seguir siendo responsables del daño que ayudan a causar.

En los últimos años, las organizaciones han intentado formalizar este deber mediante códigos de conducta y supervisión independiente. Los críticos sostienen que tales medidas pueden convertirse en una forma de tranquilidad más que en una rendición de cuentas genuina, sobre todo cuando rara vez se aplican sanciones. Un enfoque más duradero, según sugieren muchos filósofos, consistiría en cultivar el hábito de preguntarse quién podría verse afectado por una decisión antes de tomarla, y no después de que se haya producido el daño.
